analysis.title: Not The Fed You Are Looking For
key_insights: TS Lombard argues central banks have promised a return to 2% inflation 'next year' for five years, and most sellside 2027 outlooks again assume this.
Inflation began moving the wrong way in 2026 and the labour market stabilized then reaccelerated, so central banks could no longer argue policy was restrictive enough and had to start raising rates.
Fed Chair Warsh has talked tough on inflation and reaffirmed the 2% target, but has raised rates only once, by 25bps, and passed on chances to surprise the market.
In the October press conference Warsh said the economy was not 'overheating' or 'running too hot' while still threatening to hike, which TSL says undermines the hawkish rhetoric.
TSL reads Warsh as believing talk plus token hikes can lower inflation without restraining demand, relying on the 'expectations fairy'.
TSL says an honest Warsh would signal one 25bps hike in December and another in Q1, which it describes as the FOMC consensus.
TSL's own view is that inflation and employment data will force far more, with 25bps every quarter until something breaks and inflation is back on track.

macro_indicators.reading: One 25bps hike in December and another in Q1 (FOMC consensus as TSL describes it)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Base case is a slow, token hiking path, which TSL thinks is insufficient.
TSL expects more tightening than the FOMC consensus, a hawkish risk to front-end pricing.

risk_factors: Inflation persistently above 2% target with a reaccelerating labour market.
Fed credibility risk if token hikes fail to anchor expectations.
Eventual forced larger tightening could break something in markets or the economy.
vol_and_positioning: The market priced a non-zero chance of a hike on several occasions since the summer and the FOMC did not deliver, so surprise hikes have been avoided.
cross_bank_references: Most sellside economists continue to believe central banks will return inflation to target next year.

key_data_points.metric: Size of the only Warsh Fed rate hike so far
key_data_points.anchor: he has raised interest rates only once, by just 25bps

key_data_points.context: Until something breaks and inflation is back on the right path
key_data_points.anchor: 25bps EVERY QUARTER until something genuinely “breaks”, and inflation is back on the right path.

tension_points.bull_case: FOMC consensus is one 25bps hike in December and another in Q1, with Warsh's tough talk expected to anchor expectations.
tension_points.bear_case: TSL says inflation and employment data will force far more, 25bps every quarter, because Warsh thinks the economy is not overheating and relies on the expectations fairy.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A genuine break in the economy or markets, or inflation returning to the right path, would end the hiking cycle.
